title: Leaver: offboarding and access clean-up for small companies
source: Top 25 SaaS ideas for Victor (research report, Nov 2026)
summary: When someone leaves a small company, one click removes their access to Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 and connected apps, and keeps proof that it was done.
hook: "Three months after she left, we found out our old sales manager could still log into the CRM."
story:
**Sofia is office manager at a 60-person design firm with no IT department.** When someone leaves, she disables their email, but nobody knows which other apps they used: Dropbox, a CRM, design tools, apps connected with "Sign in with Google".

Last quarter a client's security questionnaire asked: **"Can you show evidence that leavers lose access within 24 hours?"** Sofia could not. Later she found a former employee **still had access to a shared drive**. She wants a checklist that runs itself and a log that proves it.
whyNow: Insurers, auditors and customers increasingly ask for offboarding evidence as part of security checks (an inference from the insurance and questionnaire trends). There is no specific deadline.
evidence: 48% of former employees still had app access months after leaving (CloudEagle 2026 report, 1,000 enterprise CIOs and CISOs; vendor source) [CloudEagle]
A Sagiss survey, cited second-hand, found 82% of workers at firms under 250 staff had lingering access [Efficiently Connected / Infonaligy]
Torii, Zluri, BetterCloud and CloudEagle are enterprise-oriented; their prices were not found [Top 25 report]
